description_full: Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation operates in the secondary mortgage market in the United States. The company operates through two segments: Single-Family and Multifamily. The Single-Family segment purchases, securitizes, and guarantees single-family loans; and manages single-family mortgage credit and market risk, as well as manages mortgage-related investments portfolio, single-family securitization activities, and treasury functions. This segment also serves mortgage banking companies, commercial banks, regional banks, community banks, credit unions, HFAs, savings institutions, and non-depository institutions. The Multifamily segment engages in the purchase, securitization, and guarantee of multifamily loans; issuance of multifamily K certificates; manages multifamily mortgage credit and market risk; and invests in multifamily loans and mortgage-related securities. It also serves banks and other depository institutions, insurance companies, money managers, central banks, pension funds, state and local governments, REITs, non-depository institutions, and brokers and dealers. Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation was incorporated in 1970 and is headquartered in McLean, Virginia.

financial_summary: Freddie Mac is a mid-cap financial services business with a $2.6B market cap on $23.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 0% against a 12% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 15.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.2× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
